year: undated (no earlier than late 2024; cites arXiv:2411.12085, pp. 16-17)
title: New Proofs of Exact LP Reformulations for Binary Polynomial Optimization with Bounded Treewidth
contribution: Two new proofs (an extreme-point perturbation argument and a constructive complementary-slackness argument whose dual is the tree-decomposition DP) that binary polynomial optimization with treewidth d has an exact LP with O(k2^d) variables and constraints, with total dual integrality as a corollary.
problem_entry: Known theorem (Laurent 2009; Bienstock-Munoz 2018) whose proofs go by induction on tree-decomposition nodes; the note re-proves it by LP arguments and extracts TDI (pp. 4-5, 15); LP motivated by cut generation and sensitivity analysis (p. 2).
key_idea: Per-bag convex-combination multipliers, project out monomial variables, then row-reduce parent-child consistency equations so each multiplier appears in exactly one equation per pair (Claim 1, Algorithm 1, Observation 1, pp. 10-12); both proofs rest on this normal form.
assumptions: Binary variables, polynomial objective/constraints (p. 1); a tree decomposition of the associated graph of width d with k nodes is given (pp. 3-4); each constraint's support lies in one bag and per-bag feasible binary points are enumerated (pp. 6-7).
proof_devices: fractional extreme point written as midpoint of two points via +-eps perturbations propagated root to leaves (pp. 12-13)
dual of LP solved bottom-up by DP min-recursion, integral primal set top-down from active dual constraints, complementary slackness (pp. 13-15)
TDI corollary from integral constructed duals (p. 15)
reverse induction on row-operation iterations for Claim 1 (pp. 10-11)
running example threaded through all steps (Examples 1-6, pp. 5-15)
positioning: Alternative to the inductive proofs of Laurent (2009) and Bienstock-Munoz (2018); related to Wainwright-Jordan Sherali-Adams treewidth exactness and Faenza et al., Del Pia-Khajavirad, Cifuentes-Dey-Xu (p. 4); DP polyhedral view of Martin-Rardin-Campbell (p. 2).
writing: Short note without a conclusion; heavy reliance on a running example; Proof 1 is a sketch at the propagation step (p. 13); abstract says O(n2^d) vs Theorem 1 O(k2^d) (pp. 1, 4); running-example coefficient -5 drifts to +1 in Examples 3, 4, 6 (pp. 5, 9, 12, 15).
limits_future: No future directions, no tightness or lower-bound discussion of the O(k2^d) size, no cost of finding the decomposition (pp. 1-15; text ends at Corollary 2, p. 15).

method_links.note: IP-polyhedral tools (extreme points, LP duality, TDI, DP as polyhedron) carried to BPO; each bag's multilinear set convexified jointly
re-proof note gives no tight example, lower bound or failure case; boundary treatment absent outside headline papers

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Re-prove a known theorem through LP duality to expose the algorithm as the dual
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: DP over the tree decomposition is the dual of the exact LP; constructive complementary slackness proves integrality and yields TDI

transferable: Prove integrality of a tree-structured polytope by +-eps perturbations propagated from root to leaves, writing a fractional point as the midpoint of two feasible points (pp. 12-13).

Construct the dual bottom-up by the DP min-recursion and an integral primal top-down from active dual constraints, then verify complementary slackness; integral duals give a TDI corollary (pp. 13-15).
Row-reduce coupling equations so each variable appears once per parent-child block before any perturbation or duality argument (pp. 10-12).
Thread one small running example through every reformulation and both proofs, and re-check its coefficients against the original objective (pp. 5-15).
coauthors: Sourabh K. Choudhary, Nikolaos V. Sahinidis

quotes.text: the first proof shows that a fractional feasible solution of the LP can be expressed as an average of two distinct feasible points, thereby proving that fractional points cannot be extreme points, and hence integrality of the LP.
The dual to the LP is the DP formulation for solving such problems over known tree decompositions.
